caps.GA_measured_tree: driver argv/env contains /review/moqls8-strengthened-parent-replay-v1/ plus ppid descendants; counted=max(declared,measured)

sequence: tiny controls each run, then items in order from --start-at; continue only after PASS; gate wait up to 1200 s only for the GA lane-RSS condition
acceptance_per_item: bound formula identity (own 22-MATCH hash/bytes) before feeding; both feeds measured complete; kissat rc20 and status lines exactly [s UNSATISFIABLE] (CR-strip only); drat-trim rc0 and exactly [s VERIFIED]; only tolerated warning class = drat-trim duplicate-literal normalisation (counted; baseline 375334 recorded); any other WARNING/early EOF/less-than-expected fails; proof relay read==relayed with sha256/bytes; raw kissat log and raw drat-trim stream sha256/bytes; wall/RSS; any stop = UNKNOWN
scope: WORKER results only; not parent-qualified; no S6 GB
ga_priority: launch only when no GA desk driver alive and no unknown GA reading; wait until 17:29 cutoff; running pipeline finishes (N8ReplayV5 protocol)
switch_plan: run-a1 (r3) stopped by driver SIGTERM at the next item boundary; any item started by r3 after the boundary is UNKNOWN and rerun under r4 with a new run tag
hold_protocol: on GA HOLD message the worker x-creates hold/HOLD-<n>.json; on RELEASE x-creates hold/RELEASE-<n>.json; gate requires holds<=releases; running pipeline finishes; no boundary SIGTERM
staged_transport: kissat alone (DRAT FIFO -> collector -> driver RAM chunks, sha/bytes); then drat-trim alone fed CNF + in-memory proof (fed sha/bytes == collected); proof never on disk
motivation: concurrent r4/r5 aggregate peaks 5.94 GB (P0-B6) and 6.08 GB (P2-C3) vs 6 GiB cap; kissat maxrss up to 4.33 GB and drat-trim up to 3.58 GB; staging bounds peak by the larger stage plus the proof buffer
status: FROZEN, NOT RUN; offered to parent; use only on explicit parent GO
concurrency: GA counted (max(declared 4.6 GiB, measured)) + GB cap 6 GiB <= 11 GiB; GA running allowed; HOLD markers still block
caveat: safe for GA only if the GA desk in-flight rule also uses the 11 GiB lane limit (not 7.85 GiB)
